intro: The Oracle at Delphi has stopped answering questions. Instead she has left a set of riddles, each one sworn upon a different god, and the pilgrims have learned to wait in the same hush as the priests who tend the sacred hearth. Each evening the elders clear the temple steps of the day's offerings, and each evening they find one more fig than they left, one more coin than the pilgrims brought, one more shadow at the edge of the ash-tray where no one sits. They do not speak of it; they sweep it into the same cloth and carry it down the Sacred Way as though it were always so. The pilgrims have begun to leave small gifts of their own, not for the goddess, but for whichever thing comes after dark and takes the extra things.
echo: The gods live nearly three thousand metres up, above the clouds of Thessaly.
